narrative.overview:
Epoch is a well-kept reading room for one family's history. Pages are warm cream paper rather than white, text is set in archival stone inks rather than grey, and a single deep emerald, the colour of a cloth book binding, marks the few things that act. The welcome page is the only place the room is shown literally: a library photograph under an emerald wash, with the mark and the tagline in vellum. Everywhere else the archive is implied by material and restraint, not by ornament.

The mood is calm and scholarly, warm rather than clinical, and approachable for relatives who are not researchers. Record pages are dense and quiet: small type, uppercase section labels, bordered sections, plain links. Detail is welcome; decoration is not. Warmth comes from the cream and stone palette instead of the white-and-slate of enterprise tools, so the app feels like the family's own. Touch targets grow on coarse pointers and dialog fields never trigger a phone's zoom, so the people who visit occasionally are not punished for it.

The tree canvas is the one place colour carries data. There the archive gives way to a chart table: a slightly darker paper with a dot grid, person cards tinted by a muted sex palette plus a symbol, and parent-child lines distinguished by line style first and hue second.
keyCharacteristics: Cream paper surfaces (`page-cream`, `panel-cream`, `dialog-cream`); white is reserved for what you scan or type into: list panels, tables and fields.
Stone inks for all text and rules; emerald for action and the brand only.
One system sans stack at small sizes; hierarchy comes from weight and uppercase labels.
Flat by default: borders and tonal steps carry structure, shadows mean "floating".
Light theme only. There is no dark mode.
Lucide line icons at 14–16px beside labels.

rules.name: The One Binding Rule
rules.body: Emerald is the only saturated colour in the chrome. It marks what acts (primary buttons, links, the selected row, focus) and the brand mark, and nothing else. A second accent in the chrome is a defect.

rules.name: The Paper, Not White Rule
rules.body: The page and its chrome are cream; section cards are stone-washed. Pure white is earned by content you scan or type into: fields, list panels and tables.

rules.name: The Line Before Hue Rule
rules.body: On the tree, a relationship type is told by line style first and colour second, and a person's sex by a symbol as well as a tint. Nothing on the canvas depends on colour alone.

rules.name: The Weight Not Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy inside the app comes from weight (400, 600, 700) and the uppercase section label, not from large type. Nothing in the app chrome exceeds 1.5rem; the display size belongs to the splash.

rules.name: The Sixteen-Pixel Field Rule
rules.body: On a coarse pointer every input, select and textarea renders at 16px or larger, so iOS never zooms when a dialog focuses a field.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface that sits on the page has a border and nothing heavier than the hairline. A real shadow means the element floats above the page: a header, a floating control, a dialog, a drawer.

rules.name: The Translucent Chrome Rule
rules.body: Chrome that overlays content (the sticky header, the drawer) is panel or dialog cream at 90–98% with a backdrop blur, so the record scrolls visibly underneath.

dos: **Do** use page cream (`#fcf9f2`) for the page, stone wash for section cards, and white for fields, list panels and tables.
**Do** keep emerald-800 as the only fill for primary actions, with emerald-700 for hover and focus.
**Do** open every record section with the uppercase 0.75rem bold stone-600 section label.
**Do** use the `focus-ring`, `focus-ring-inset`, `focus-input` and `menu-item` utilities instead of new focus styles.
**Do** give touch screens 44px targets with the `coarse:` variant, and keep fields at 16px there.
**Do** pair every colour on the tree with a second signal: a symbol for sex, a line style for the parent-child type, a dashed edge for privacy.
**Do** add new tree colours to `tree-tokens.ts` so the contrast tests cover them.
donts: **Don't** introduce a second accent colour in the chrome; amber is for notices and red for errors.
**Don't** give cards or panels that sit on the page more than the hairline shadow; a real shadow means the element floats.
**Don't** use blue or pink for parent-child lines; they would read as sex.
**Don't** set app-chrome text larger than 1.5rem; the display size belongs to the splash.
**Don't** name a global class `.card`, `.btn`, `.link` or `.heading`; components scope those names, and a global rule would leak into them.
**Don't** use a white page background, or white for section cards; white is for fields, list panels and tables.
